sections.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief

tracks.title: Welcome — a hospital that became a museum
tracks.where: Play this just inside the Sabatini entrance on Calle Santa Isabel, Floor 1, between the two glass lift towers that frame the doorway. You don't need to stand anywhere in particular.
tracks.what: The Sabatini Building: Madrid's eighteenth-century Hospital General, largely designed by Francesco Sabatini, opened as the Centro de Arte Reina Sofía in 1986 and established as the Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía in 1988. Route of this guide: Floor 1, Floor 2, Floor 4, Nouvel roof terrace.
tracks.listen: How an unfinished royal hospital escaped demolition and became Spain's national museum of modern art, and how this guide will walk you through it.

tracks.title: Garden · Extra · Gargallo's Great Prophet and Chillida
tracks.where: In the garden in the middle of the Sabatini Building, reached from the cloister on Floor 1. Look for a tall dark bronze figure, well over two metres high, if it is on display here, and for two rust-brown steel crosses curving into each other, about three metres long.
tracks.what: Pablo Gargallo, Grand prophète (Great Prophet), 1933, cast 1936, sand-cast bronze, 236 × 75 × 45 cm. Eduardo Chillida, Toki egin, Homenaje a San Juan de la Cruz (Toki egin, Homage to San Juan de la Cruz), 1989–1990, cast Corten steel, 142 × 295 × 213 cm, Exhibited in Sabatini Building, Garden.
tracks.listen: The one courtyard of Sabatini's hospital that was actually built, a prophet made of air as much as bronze, and two steel crosses that embrace.

tracks.title: Room 102 · Richard Serra — Equal-Parallel: Guernica-Bengasi
tracks.where: Room 102 on Floor 1, a long white gallery with a barrel-vaulted ceiling. On the floor stand four solid blocks of dark weathering steel, about one and a half metres high, two square and two long, set in a line with an empty gap in the middle.
tracks.what: Richard Serra, Equal-Parallel: Guernica-Bengasi, 1986, cast Corten steel, four parts, each 148.5 cm high (two 500 cm long, two 148.5 cm), made for the Reina Sofía's opening exhibition. Also in the room: Richard Serra, Inversion, 2001, two forged steel blocks.
tracks.listen: Why a sculpture of four steel blocks carries the names of two bombings, and how it turns an old hospital ward into a space you feel with your body.

tracks.title: Room 201.01 · Holy Bohemia — From Slum to Gran Vía
tracks.where: Room 201.01 on Floor 2, the first collection room, titled 'Holy Bohemia. From Slum to Gran Vía'. Look for a black-and-white photograph of King Alfonso XIII opening the Madrid Metro, and Ricardo Baroja's small, dark etchings of the city's edges.
tracks.what: Room 201.01, 'Holy Bohemia. From Slum to Gran Vía'. Alfonso Sánchez García, Alfonso XIII inaugura el primer tramo del metropolitano de Madrid (Alfonso XIII Opens the First Section of the Madrid Underground System), 17 October 1919, posthumous print 1984, gelatin silver print. Ricardo Baroja, El suburbio (The Suburb), 1909, etching and aquatint. Floor 2 presentation: 'Avant-garde Territories: City, Architecture and Magazines'.
tracks.listen: How Madrid's painters moved from the slums and taverns of a country in crisis to the concrete towers and metro of a modern city.

tracks.title: Room 201.02 · Picasso — Woman in Blue
tracks.where: Room 201.02, 'Holy Bohemia. Paris was a party'. Find Picasso's large portrait, over a metre tall, of a woman dressed in blue, standing and filling the canvas.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, Mujer en azul (Woman in Blue), Madrid, 1901, oil on canvas, 133 × 100 cm.
tracks.listen: The painting a nineteen-year-old Picasso sent to a Madrid exhibition and then walked away from, and what he borrowed from the masters to make it.

tracks.title: Room 201.02 · Extra · Ramon Casas and Isidre Nonell — Barcelona, Paris and the poster
tracks.where: Stay in Room 201.02. Look for Ramon Casas's tall Anís del Mono posters, more than two metres high, each with a large woman against flat, bold colour, and for Isidre Nonell's heavy, thickly painted figures of women.
tracks.what: Ramon Casas, Anís del Mono. «Mono y mona» (Anís del Mono. "Male Monkey and Female Monkey"), 1898, lithograph on paper, 212 × 103 cm, and other Anís del Mono posters. Isidre Nonell, Mujer (Woman), 1907, oil on canvas, 63 × 52 cm.
tracks.listen: Two Barcelona artists of 1900: one selling anise from the street wall, one painting the people the city preferred not to see.

tracks.title: Room 201.03 · José Gutiérrez Solana — The Gathering at the Café de Pombo
tracks.where: Room 201.03, 'Holy Bohemia. Ramón Gómez de la Serna, the improbable artist'. Find the large group portrait, about two metres wide, of men gathered round a café table, with one man standing in the centre.
tracks.what: José Gutiérrez Solana, La tertulia del Café de Pombo (The Gathering at the Café de Pombo), 1920, oil on canvas, 161.5 × 211.5 cm, donated by Ramón Gómez de la Serna, 1947. Also in the room: Rafael Barradas, Pombo.
tracks.listen: The Saturday gatherings at a Madrid café where the avant-garde talked, and the host who gave the painting of his own party away.

tracks.title: Room 201.04 · Extra · José Ortiz Echagüe — photographs of Spain
tracks.where: Room 201.04, 'José Ortiz Echagüe', a small room of five works. Look for his black-and-white prints of village life, with deep, velvety blacks, such as a sermon in a village church, and sculpted busts by Julio Antonio.
tracks.what: José Ortiz Echagüe, Sermón en la aldea (Village Sermon), 1903, direct carbon print on laid paper, image 40.5 × 38.7 cm; also Lagarteranas and Lagarteranas en misa. Julio Antonio, Mujer de la mantilla and Moza de Aldea del Rey.
tracks.listen: A photographer who wanted his pictures to feel like travelling back in time, and printed them so heavily by hand that a critic objected.

tracks.title: Room 202.01 · Rafael Barradas — Atocha, and Madrid, a Diverse City
tracks.where: Room 202.01, 'Madrid, a Diverse City'. Find Barradas's Atocha, a small canvas just over half a metre wide, its busy street scene broken into overlapping, fragmented shapes. María Blanchard's tall Girl at Her First Communion, almost two metres high, is in the same room.
tracks.what: Rafael Barradas, Atocha, 1919, oil on canvas, 53 × 66 cm. Also: María Blanchard, La comulgante (Girl at Her First Communion), 1914, oil on canvas, 180 × 124 cm.
tracks.listen: How a painter from Uruguay decided a modern city should vibrate, and how planners set out to rebuild the crowded cities of Europe.

tracks.title: Room 202.02 · Sonia Delaunay — Dubonnet, and Barcelona, Neutral City
tracks.where: Room 202.02, 'Barcelona, Neutral City'. Find Sonia Delaunay's Dubonnet, a canvas about three-quarters of a metre wide that looks like a poster, built from bold colour and big letters, with a line of small lettering along the bottom. Olga Sacharoff's portrait of Arthur Cravan, with a cat, is in the same room.
tracks.what: Sonia Delaunay, Dubonnet, 1914, water-based paint on canvas, 61 × 76 cm. Also: Olga Sacharoff, Joven del gato (retrato de Arthur Cravan) (Youth of the Cat [Portrait of Arthur Cravan]), c. 1916, oil and collage on canvas, 111 × 94 cm.
tracks.listen: A "poster" that nobody commissioned, and the circle of avant-garde artists who sat out the First World War in Barcelona.

tracks.title: Room 202.03 · Joan Miró — House with Palm Tree, and the Dalmau Gallery
tracks.where: Room 202.03, 'Dalmau Gallery'. Find Miró's House with Palm Tree, a canvas about three-quarters of a metre wide: a country farmhouse with a palm tree, plants drawn in fine detail and ploughed land kept simple. Picabia's Totalisateur, a watercolour and ink drawing of a puzzling machine, is in the same room.
tracks.what: Joan Miró, La casa de la palmera (House with Palm Tree), 1918, oil on canvas, 65 × 73 cm. Also: Francis Picabia, Totalisateur (Totalizer), c. 1922, watercolour and ink on paperboard, 55 × 73 cm.
tracks.listen: The farmhouse painting that went to Paris to launch Miró and sold nothing, and the Barcelona dealer whose walls held both Miró and Picabia's machines.

tracks.title: Room 204.01 · Picasso — Head of a Woman (Fernande), and Cubism
tracks.where: Room 204.01, 'Cubism, the First International Language'. Find Picasso's bronze head, about forty centimetres high, its face, hair and neck made of swelling, interlocking forms. A painting with the same title, a head broken into sharp planes in browns, greens and greys, is in the same room.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, Tête de femme (Fernande) (Woman's Head [Fernande]), autumn 1909, patinated bronze, lost-wax cast, 41.3 × 24.7 × 26.6 cm. Also: Pablo Picasso, Tête de femme (Fernande), Paris, 1909–1910, oil on canvas, 61 × 50 cm. Room 204.01 also includes works lent by the Telefónica Collection.
tracks.listen: How a bronze head travelled from Paris to New York and signalled the birth of Cubist sculpture, and how Cubism was mocked before it conquered.

tracks.title: Room 204.02 · Juan Gris — Portrait of Josette Gris, and María Blanchard
tracks.where: Room 204.02, 'Cubism, the First International Language'. Find Gris's portrait of a seated woman, over a metre tall, built from calm, clear planes, her hands crossed in her lap. María Blanchard's larger, near-abstract Cubist Composition, in lemon yellow, pink, orange and green, is in the same room.
tracks.what: Juan Gris, Portrait de Madame Josette Gris (Portrait of Madame Josette Gris), October 1916, oil on board, 116 × 73 cm, donation of Douglas Cooper. Also: María Blanchard, Composición cubista (Cubist Composition), 1916–1919, oil and collage on canvas, 154 × 114 cm.
tracks.listen: Two Spanish painters in wartime Paris: Gris making Cubism calm and architectural, Blanchard making it dizzying.

tracks.title: Room 204.03 · Juan Gris — The Open Window, and After Cubism
tracks.where: Room 204.03, 'After Cubism'. Find Gris's Open Window, a horizontal canvas a metre wide, where a room and the view through its window meet in one picture. Oskar Schlemmer's works for the Triadic Ballet and the Bauhaus dances, posters, figures and photographs from the 1920s, are in the same room.
tracks.what: Juan Gris, La fenêtre ouverte (Open Window), January–March 1921, oil on canvas, 66 × 100 cm. Also: Oskar Schlemmer, Das Triadische Ballett, Der Abstrakte (The Triadic Ballet, The Abstract), 1922, and other Triadic Ballet and Bauhaus works, 1922–1928.
tracks.listen: Why Gris painted window after window by the sea at Bandol, and how the room's title came from a 1918 manifesto that tried to tidy up after Cubism.

tracks.title: Room 205.02 · Extra · GATEPAC — architecture for a new republic
tracks.where: Room 205.02, a room of architects' plans, photographs and photomontages. Look for the Pla Macià material by Le Corbusier and the Catalan group, and Man Ray's photographic portrait of Picasso.
tracks.what: Room 205.02, 'GATEPAC, The Urgency of Facilities': Le Corbusier and GATCPAC, Pla Macià. Una casa, un árbol (Pla Macià. A House, a Tree); photomontages and advertising by Pere Català Pic and Josep Sala; Man Ray, Portrait de Picasso. Also Room 205.01: Josep Torres Clavé and Josep Lluís Sert, Hospital para tuberculosos de 400 camas HT400.
tracks.listen: How a group of young architects asked for "everything but decoration", and what the new Republic asked of them.

tracks.title: Room 205.04 · Extra · John Heartfield — 33 photomontages
tracks.where: Room 205.04, a room of black-and-white photomontages: book covers, magazine pages and election posters with German slogans. Look for the Communist Party poster 'The Hand Has 5 Fingers', built around an outstretched hand.
tracks.what: John Heartfield, John Heartfield. 33 Fotomontagen (John Heartfield. 33 Photomontages), portfolio published 1974; including 5 Finger hat die Hand. Mit 5 packst Du den Feind! Wählt Liste 5. Kommunistische Partei! (The Hand Has 5 Fingers. With 5 You Seize the Enemy. Vote List 5. Communist Party!), 1928 / edition of 1974, phototype on paper, 64 x 48 cm.
tracks.listen: Why Heartfield left the cuts in his photomontages showing, and how he shaped the Spanish posters next door.

tracks.title: Room 205.05 · Speaking Walls — Josep Renau and the Civil War poster
tracks.where: Room 205.05, 'Speaking Walls', hung with Civil War posters and magazine pages. Look for Josep Renau's wide horizontal photomontage poster, about a metre across, with the Catalan title Obrers, camperols, soldats, intel·lectuals.
tracks.what: Josep Renau, Obrers, camperols, soldats, intel.lectuals (Workers, Peasants, Soldiers, Intellectuals), 1937, photolithography on paper, 75 x 107 cm. Also: Renau, Los marinos de Cronstadt (The Kronstadt Sailors); Arturo Ballester, 19 julio 1936; José Bardasano and Juana Francisca poster; Umbral magazine posters.
tracks.listen: How posters turned the streets of the Republic into a stage, and how the man behind one of them set Guernica in motion.

tracks.title: Room 205.06 · Ángeles Santos — A World
tracks.where: Room 205.06, 'Realism and Superrealism in New Art'. Find the largest canvas in the room, about three metres each way: a square, box-like world floating in a dark sky, its surfaces crowded with tiny houses and figures.
tracks.what: Ángeles Santos, Un mundo (A World), 1929, Valladolid, oil on canvas, 290 x 310 cm. Also in the room: Ángeles Santos, Tertulia (The Gathering), 1929.
tracks.listen: How a seventeen-year-old in Valladolid painted a whole world from a book and some magazines, and stunned Madrid.

tracks.title: Room 205.06 · Maruja Mallo — The Fair, and Dalí — Figure at a Window
tracks.where: Still in Room 205.06. Mallo's La verbena is a wide, crowded, brightly coloured fairground scene. Dalí's Figura en una finestra is a calm, upright picture of a young woman seen from behind, leaning at a window over a blue bay.
tracks.what: Maruja Mallo, La verbena (The Fair), 1927 (September), oil on canvas, 119 x 165 cm. Salvador Dalí, Figura en una finestra (Figure at the Window), 1925, oil on papier-mâché, 105 x 74.5 cm.
tracks.listen: Two young painters of the same moment: one throws a whole fair at you, the other paints a silence.

tracks.title: Room 205.07 · Extra · Gecé — The Sewer Inspector
tracks.where: Room 205.07, a small room of paintings, posters and architecture photographs around the magazine La Gaceta Literaria. Look for the photographs of plans for a restaurant on Monte Ulía, and Cassandre's poster Étoile du Nord.
tracks.what: Room 205.07, 'Gecé: The Sewer Inspector', on Ernesto Giménez Caballero and La Gaceta Literaria: José Manuel Aizpurúa and Joaquín Labayen, Restaurante en Monte Ulía (Restaurant on Mount Ulia), 1927, photographs of plans; Cassandre, Étoile du Nord; Norah Borges, Campesinas de Portugal (Peasant Women from Portugal); Alfonso Ponce de León, Arquitectura urbana (Urban Architecture).
tracks.listen: The man behind a key magazine of Spanish modernity, and how his politics left him writing it alone.

tracks.title: Room 205.09 · The 1937 Spanish Pavilion — Calder's Mercury Fountain and the pavilion model
tracks.where: Room 205.09, 'The International Exposition of 1937: Architecture, Art and Propaganda', the room just before Guernica. Find the large architectural model of a low, modern pavilion, over two metres long, and Calder's fountain maquette: a low basin with a mobile above it carrying a red disc and the word ALMADEN.
tracks.what: Alexander Calder, Mercury Fountain (Maquette), 1937 / 1943, assemblage of plywood, paperboard, iron sheet, tin, steel wire and paint, 88 x 105.5 x 106 cm, 1:3 scale model, long-term loan of the Calder Foundation, New York. Josep Lluís Sert and Luis Lacasa, Maqueta del Pabellón de España en la Exposición Internacional de París de 1937 (Spanish Pavilion Model for the International Exhibition of Paris, 1937), 1987, model by Juan Mirón. Also: Picasso, two horse studies for Guernica; Solana, Procesión de la muerte; Horacio Ferrer, Madrid 1937 (Aviones negros).
tracks.listen: What the Spanish Republic built in Paris in the middle of a war, and why a fountain of mercury stood beside Guernica.

tracks.title: Room 205.09 · Extra · Joan Miró — Aidez l'Espagne and Portrait II
tracks.where: Still in Room 205.09. Aidez l'Espagne is a small print, about the size of a sheet of notepaper: a figure raising a huge fist, with the words "Aidez l'Espagne". Portrait II is a large canvas, over one and a half metres tall, with two rounded shapes in broad, calm areas of colour.
tracks.what: Joan Miró, Aidez L'Espagne (Help Spain), 1937, stencilling on paper, image 29.3 x 21 cm. Joan Miró, Portrait II, 1938 (11 June), oil on canvas, 162 x 130 cm.
tracks.listen: What survives of Miró's work for the 1937 pavilion, and how his painting calmed as the war went on.

tracks.title: Room 205.10 · Pablo Picasso — Guernica
tracks.where: Room 205.10, 'Guernica'. The painting fills one long wall: almost 3.5 metres high and nearly 7.8 metres wide, entirely in black, white and grey. Stand well back, towards the middle of the room, to take in the whole of it.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, Guernica, 1937 (1 May – 4 June, Paris), oil on canvas, 349.3 x 776.6 cm, registration DE00050, entered the museum in 1992.
tracks.listen: How a commission for a world's fair became a painting about war itself, and why it hangs in this particular room.

tracks.title: Room 205.10 · Picasso's sketches for Guernica, and Dora Maar's photographs
tracks.where: Still in Room 205.10, at the small framed works shown near Guernica: Picasso's preparatory drawings, a few of them in colour, and Dora Maar's small black-and-white photographs of the canvas in his studio.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, Hombre cayendo. Dibujo preparatorio para «Guernica» (Man Falling. Sketch for "Guernica"), 1937 (27 May, Paris), graphite and gouache on tracing cloth, 23.2 x 29.3 cm, Picasso Bequest; also Madre con niño muerto en escalera (I) (Mother with Dead Child on Ladder [I]), Cabeza de caballo (I) (Horse Head [I]), Estudio para la cabeza del toro (Study for Bull's Head), Estudio para mano (Study for a Hand). Dora Maar, Reportage sur l'évolution de «Guernica» (Photo Report of the Evolution of "Guernica"), 1937 (May–June, Paris), gelatin silver prints, each about 12 x 18 cm.
tracks.listen: How Guernica changed while it was being painted, caught by Picasso's own drawings and by Dora Maar's camera.

tracks.title: Room 205.11 · The Spanish Night — María Blanchard, Woman with a Fan
tracks.where: Room 205.11, 'The Spanish Night. Flamenco, Avant-garde and Popular Culture'. Find a tall Cubist canvas, about 1.6 metres high, of a woman broken into overlapping coloured planes, a fan among them.
tracks.what: María Blanchard, Mujer con abanico (Woman with a Fan), 1913–1915, oil on canvas, 161 x 97 cm. Also in the room: Man Ray, Vicente Escudero, bailaor de flamenco (Vicente Escudero, Flamenco Dancer); Natalia Goncharova, Costume espagnole (Spanish Costume) designs; Joan Miró, Danseuse espagnole I (Spanish Dancer I); Salvador Dalí, Gitano de Figueres (Roma Man from Figueres); Jacques Lipchitz, Figure with Guitar.
tracks.listen: How flamenco fed the avant-garde, and how a Cubist woman with a fan helped drive María Blanchard out of Madrid.

tracks.title: Room 205.12 · Extra · Alberto — The Pilgrimage of Cuckolds
tracks.where: Room 205.12, a small room about dance and the stage: Alberto's designs for the ballet, a Castilian man's costume made for it, and Carlos Sáenz de Tejada's small models of a dancer, a guitarist, a hand-clapper and a bullfighter.
tracks.what: Alberto (Alberto Sánchez), La romería de los cornudos (The Pilgrimage of Cuckolds), 1933, set and costume designs; Anonymous, Traje masculino castellano «paleto», para la obra escénica «La Romería de los Cornudos» (Spanish "Yokel" Men's Suit for the Play "The Pilgrimage of Cuckolds"); Carlos Sáenz de Tejada, La bailaora (maqueta), El guitarrista (maqueta), El palmero (maqueta), El torero (maqueta), and designs for La Argentina's Ballets Espagnols.
tracks.listen: How two dancers renewed Spanish dance, and how a sculptor turned the stage into a dry Castilian dreamscape.

tracks.title: Room 205.13 · Salvador Dalí — The Great Masturbator, and Breton's Surrealists
tracks.where: Room 205.13, 'André Breton. The Magician of Surrealism'. Find Dalí's wide canvas, about one and a half metres across: a huge pale head in profile with its eyes closed, a grasshopper clinging to it, under a smooth, empty sky.
tracks.what: Salvador Dalí, Visage du Grand Masturbateur (Face of the Great Masturbator), 1929, oil on canvas, 110 x 150 cm, Salvador Dalí Bequest, 1990. Also in the room: Joan Miró, Peinture (Hirondelle) (Painting [Swallow]); Pablo Picasso, La nageuse (The Swimmer) and La femme au jardin (Woman in the Garden); works by René Magritte, Max Ernst, Yves Tanguy, Victor Brauner and Francis Picabia; Dalí's poster for a Surrealist lecture cycle, «La langouste».
tracks.listen: How André Breton gathered the Surrealist painters, and what one summer with Gala did to Dalí's painting.

tracks.title: Room 205.14 · Óscar Domínguez and Gaceta de Arte
tracks.where: Room 205.14, 'Culture's Universal Time. Gaceta de Arte'. Find Domínguez's small upright canvas, about 60 by 46 centimetres: two women on a mountain top, gazing at a case of butterflies.
tracks.what: Óscar Domínguez, Papillons perdus dans la montagne (Butterflies Lost in the Mountain), 1934, oil on canvas, 61 x 46 cm. Also in the room: Domínguez, Cueva de guanches (Guanche Cave) and Pérégrinations de Georges Hugnet; Joan Miró, Femme et chien devant la lune (Woman and Dog in Front of the Moon); George Grosz; Willi Baumeister; Joaquín Torres García.
tracks.listen: How a magazine in Tenerife brought Surrealism, and André Breton himself, to the Canary Islands, and a painter's homesick picture of his father's butterflies.

tracks.title: Room 205.15 · Extra · Antoni Campañà — war photographs
tracks.where: Room 205.15, 'War photography'. The walls hold Antoni Campañà's black-and-white photographs of railway carriages and cars being painted with large anti-fascist slogans and images.
tracks.what: Antoni Campañà, photographs from the "red box", including Ferrocarriles del Norte. Pintando los trenes con propaganda antifascista (La tierra es tuya: Trabájala) (Railways of the North. Painting Trains with Anti-Fascist Propaganda [The Land Is Yours: Work It]); Ferrocarriles M. Z. A. Propaganda antifascista (Los aplastaremos) (We Will Crush Them); Coche intervenido por el Sindicato de dibujantes (A Car Painted by the Union of Draughtsmen); Vagón con propaganda antifascista (Los cuatro jinetes del Apocalipsis).
tracks.listen: A box of photographs that came back to light in 2018, and the trains the Republic turned into moving posters.

tracks.title: Room 205.16 · Robert Capa — war photography
tracks.where: Room 205.16, 'War photography', the larger of the two photography rooms. Look for Robert Capa's black-and-white prints, among them the militiaman falling backwards on a hillside, and children outside a house riddled with bullet holes.
tracks.what: Robert Capa, Death of a Loyalist Militiaman (near Espejo, Córdoba front), 1936 (early September) / posthumous print 1998, gelatin silver print, 31.8 x 45.4 cm; Children Outside a Bullet-Riddled Building Following an Air Raid at 10 Peironcely Street (Vallecas, Madrid), 1936 (November–December) / posthumous print 1998; Loyalist Militiaman, 1936 (August); Bilbao, mayo 1937; Barcelona, enero 1939; Farewell ceremony for the International Brigades, Les Masies; all donated by Cornell Capa, 1998. Also: Juan Miguel Pando Barrero, Refugiados en la estación de metro Sevilla, Madrid and Bombardeo nocturno en la plaza Antón Martín, Madrid.
tracks.listen: How Robert Capa and his colleagues made the Spanish Civil War the war that shaped photojournalism, and the Madrid street in one of his pictures.

tracks.title: Room 205.17 · La Barraca and the Pedagogical Missions — Dalí's portrait of Luis Buñuel
tracks.where: Room 205.17, 'Culture's Proletarians. La Barraca and the Pedagogical Missions'. Find Dalí's portrait of Buñuel, about 70 by 60 centimetres: a dark-haired young man, head and shoulders, set sharply against a landscape of tiny buildings under a cloudy sky.
tracks.what: Salvador Dalí, Retrato de Luis Buñuel (Portrait of Luis Buñuel), 1924, oil on canvas, 70 x 60 cm. Also in the room: Benjamín Palencia, Boceto para decorado de «La Barraca» (Sketch for a "La Barraca" Set) and Máscara. Cartel de «La Barraca» (Mask. "La Barraca" Poster); Francis Pitti (Bartolozzi) and Pedro Lozano, Dama. Misiones Pedagógicas (Lady. Pedagogical Missions) and Caballero en verde (Gentleman in Green); Dalí, La carreta (The Cart).
tracks.listen: Two Republican projects that took theatre, cinema and art to the villages of Spain, and a portrait of a friendship from the Residencia de Estudiantes.

tracks.title: Room 206.01 · Maruja Mallo and the School of Vallecas
tracks.where: Room 206.01, 'They say city and I reply… countryside', a small room of earthy, dark-toned paintings and sculpture. Find Maruja Mallo's Tierra y excrementos, a small picture on paperboard, about 43 by 55 centimetres, in sombre browns.
tracks.what: Maruja Mallo, Tierra y excrementos (Earth and Excrement), from the series Cloacas y campanarios (Sewers and Bell Towers), 1932 (April), oil on paperboard, 43 x 55 cm. Also in the room: Alberto Sánchez, Maternidad (Maternity); Benjamín Palencia, Composición (Composition), Peces blancos (White Fish), Toros (Tauromaquia); Antonio Rodríguez Luna, Pájaros en el melonar (Birds in the Melon Field); José Moreno Villa, Pareja (Couple).
tracks.listen: Why two artists turned their backs on the city and walked out into the dry hills east of Madrid, and how Maruja Mallo followed them into the earth.

tracks.title: Room 206.02 · Documents — Picasso, Miró, Dalí and the magazine of Georges Bataille
tracks.where: Room 206.02, 'Documents Magazine', hung like a collage of paintings, sculpture and photographs. Find Dalí's Millet's Architectonic Angelus, an upright canvas about 73 by 60 centimetres, and Miró's large Painting (The Red Spot), almost one and a half metres tall.
tracks.what: Salvador Dalí, Ángelus arquitectónico de Millet (Millet's Architectonic Angelus), 1933, oil on canvas, 73 x 60 cm. Joan Miró, Pintura (La mancha roja) (Painting [The Red Spot]), 1925, oil and pastel on canvas, 146 x 114 cm. Man Ray and Marcel Duchamp, Élevage de poussière (Dust Breeding), 1920 / posthumous print 1982. Also: Picasso, Figure and Buste et palette (Bust and Palette); Jacques Lipchitz; Brassaï; Jean Arp, Objects Placed According to the Laws of Chance.
tracks.listen: The magazine described as a war machine against preconceived ideas, and the artists who joined it against Breton.

tracks.title: Room 206.03 · Joan Miró — Pastorale, and Carl Einstein
tracks.where: Room 206.03, 'Carl Einstein. The Masses Are the Artist', the last room on this floor, with African masks, Cubist paintings and Civil War photographs. Find Miró's Pastorale, a wide canvas about 60 by 92 centimetres, in black chalk and oil, with a scatter of small signs.
tracks.what: Joan Miró, Pastorale (Pastoral), 1923–1924, black chalk and oil on canvas, 60 x 92 cm. Also in the room: Pablo Picasso, Instruments de musique sur une table (Musical Instruments on a Table); Juan Gris, Arlequin au violon (Harlequin with Violin); Salvador Dalí, sketch for L'homme invisible (The Invisible Man); George Grosz, Spain; Agustí Centelles, photographs of Buenaventura Durruti's column and of Durruti's burial; African masks collected by Carl Einstein.
tracks.listen: A critic who fought in the Civil War and believed that looking is a kind of combat, and the picture where Miró's own language of signs was born.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 1 · Juan Genovés — Document No…, and the Spanish Transition
tracks.where: Room 1, the first of the three introduction rooms that sit between the two lifts at the front of Floor 4. Find a mid-sized canvas, about 1.4 metres tall, showing a single man with his hands bound against a bare white ground.
tracks.what: Juan Genovés, Documento nº… (Document No. …), 1975, acrylic on canvas, 140 x 125 cm. Also in the room: Concha Jerez, Seguimiento de una noticia (Following a Piece of News); Picasso etchings of 1931–34. Floor intro: the three routes, the Alacena rest area.
tracks.listen: How Floor 4 works, and a painting from 1975 that was meant to be read as evidence.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 2 · Material Counterculture — La Vaquería and the Madrid of the late seventies
tracks.where: Room 2, the middle of the three introduction rooms between the lifts. Look for a set of painted chipboard panels: a dark, textured central board flanked by two drawn side boards, with small bullet marks in the surface.
tracks.what: Ceesepe (Carlos Sánchez Pérez) and Borja Satrústegui, Tableros del bar La Vaquería de la calle Libertad (Boards from the Bar La Vaquería on Calle Libertad), 1976, acrylic, black ink marker pen, pencil and coloured pencil on chipboard, 130 x 74 cm. Also: Guillermo Pérez Villalta, Escena. Personajes a la salida de un concierto de rock (Scene. Figures Leaving a Rock Concert).
tracks.listen: A bombed bar, the boards that patched its door, and how Madrid's counterculture made art outside the institutions.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 3 · Attempts at an institutional regime for art — Serra's Plaza Callao maquette and Warhol's Knives
tracks.where: Room 3, the last of the three introduction rooms, next to the second lift. Look for a small block of rust-coloured Corten steel, about 1.2 metres tall, and a large canvas of repeated kitchen knives in bright colours on a dark ground.
tracks.what: Richard Serra, Maquette for a Project in Plaza Callao, Madrid (Scale Model for Callao Square, Madrid), 1981, Corten steel, 123 x 63 x 63 cm. Andy Warhol, Knives, 1982, acrylic and screen printing ink on canvas, 176.5 x 133.4 cm. Also: Manel Armengol, Tortura / The Living Theatre (Torture / The Living Theatre), 1976.
tracks.listen: Two Americans in post-Franco Madrid: a Warhol show that put the city on the art map, and a Serra sculpture the city never got.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 4 · The Personal Is Political — Martha Rosler and Ana Mendieta
tracks.where: Room 4, just past the second lift, the first room of Route I and one of the fullest on the floor. Look for the screens: Martha Rosler's black-and-white video of a woman at a kitchen counter, and Ana Mendieta's short film of her own forearms.
tracks.what: Martha Rosler, Semiotics of the Kitchen, 1975, video, black and white, sound, 6 min 09 s. Ana Mendieta, Untitled (Blood Sign #2/Body Tracks), 1974, 8 mm film transferred to video, 1 min 20 s. Also: Hannah Wilke, Hello Boys; Eulàlia Grau, Discriminació de la dona (Discrimination of Women); Nan Goldin; Robert Mapplethorpe, Self-Portrait.
tracks.listen: How second-wave feminism put women's bodies and voices at the centre of art, from a furious cooking show to a trace of blood.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 5 · Port Activities — Gordon Matta-Clark and David Wojnarowicz
tracks.where: Room 5, next to Room 4 at the front corner of the floor. Look for a film of light pouring through cuts in the walls of an old pier building, and a series of small black-and-white photographs of a figure wearing a mask of the poet Rimbaud's face.
tracks.what: Gordon Matta-Clark, Day's End, 1975, Super 8 film transferred to video, 23 min 10 s. David Wojnarowicz, Arthur Rimbaud in New York (series), 1978–79, posthumous prints 2004, gelatin silver prints, 24.6 x 32.8 cm each.
tracks.listen: The edges of the city as places of freedom: a pier cut open to the light, and a poet's mask carried through New York.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 6 · Extra · Ruptures — Iván Zulueta's Arrebato and Madrid's junk aesthetics
tracks.where: Room 6, near the toilets on this side of the floor. Look for the screen showing Iván Zulueta's film Arrebato, the pages of Ceesepe's comic Vicios modernos, and a black-and-white photograph of a shirt lying on the ground beside a pencil sketch.
tracks.what: Iván Zulueta, Arrebato (Rapture), 1979, 35 mm film transferred to video, 110 min. Also: Alberto García-Alix, En ausencia de Willy (Willy's Absence), 1988, gelatin silver print, 37.5 x 37.1 cm; Ceesepe, Vicios modernos (Modern Vices), 1978, comic pages.
tracks.listen: The heroin years in Spain, seen from the street, and a film in which cinema itself becomes an addiction.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 7 · Las Yeguas del Apocalipsis — The Two Fridas
tracks.where: Room 7, a small room of nine works. Look for the large photograph by Las Yeguas del Apocalipsis, about 1.35 metres tall, the biggest image in the room, and a row of black-and-white photographs of the catacombs of Palermo.
tracks.what: Yeguas del Apocalipsis (Pedro Lemebel and Francisco Casas), Las dos Fridas (Two Fridas), 1989, later print 2015, inkjet print on paper, 135 x 120 cm, photograph by Pedro Marinello Kairath. Also: Peter Hujar, Palermo Catacombs #2, #3, #4, #5 and #10, 1963, gelatin silver prints; Ross Bleckner, Eulogy; Feliciano Centurión, Medusas (Jellyfish), 1994; José Leonilson, Regras de sexo seguro (Safer Sex Guidelines), 1990.
tracks.listen: How art of the AIDS years learned to speak through absence, from Hujar's catacombs to a Chilean double portrait.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 8 · Pepe Espaliú — Untitled (Three Cages)
tracks.where: Room 8, on the outer side of the floor next to Room 7. Find three long, narrow cages of black enamelled iron wire, each over seven metres long and only about half a metre across. More of Espaliú's Untitled works are in the same room.
tracks.what: Pepe Espaliú, Sin título (Tres jaulas) (Untitled [Three Cages]), 1992, welded black enamelled iron wire, dimensions variable, each part 723 x 49 x 49 cm. Also: Espaliú, further works titled Sin título (Untitled); Genín Andrada, Santiago Rodríguez, 1961, Madrid, VIH positivo desde 1984 (Santiago Rodríguez, 1961, Madrid, HIV-Positive since 1984), 1994.
tracks.listen: Three empty cages the width of a body: Espaliú's last years, the isolation of people with HIV, and the care that sustains life.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 9 · Miquel Barceló — The Specters: portraits of Hervé Guibert
tracks.where: Room 9, at the far end of Route I's outer rooms, next to Room 10. The walls hold a series of very small canvases by Miquel Barceló, each about 24 by 14 centimetres, roughly a sheet of paper folded in half: portraits of the writer Hervé Guibert.
tracks.what: Miquel Barceló, portraits of Hervé Guibert, 1990, mixed media on canvas, including L'espectre (n.º 13) (The Specter [No. 13]), 12 April 1990, 24 x 14 cm, long-term loan of the artist, 2025; Le cri paisible (n.º 23); Belfegor (n.º 4); Sin título (Untitled) nos. 2, 3, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 25. 22 works in the room.
tracks.listen: A painter and a dying writer, a red hat and two blue eyes, and how to put absence on a canvas.

tracks.section: Floor 4 · From the Transition to Grief
tracks.title: Room 10 · Juan Muñoz — The Wasteland
tracks.where: Room 10, the last room of Route I, a room of only six works. Stand at the edge of Juan Muñoz's floor piece: a wide linoleum floor with an illusionist pattern, and a bronze ventriloquist's dummy waiting in front of it.
tracks.what: Juan Muñoz, The Wasteland (Tierra baldía), 1986, bronze, wood and linoleum. Also in the room: Tony Oursler, 9/11; Susan Philipsz, Long Gone; Beatriz González, A posteriori, 2022; Carlos Rodríguez-Méndez, Región de validez (Region of Validity), 2007; Babi Badalov, Last year I and U never ever could imagine, 2020.
tracks.listen: Grief for strangers after 9/11 and the Madrid bombings, and a silent bronze dummy waiting for someone to make it speak.

tracks.title: Room 11 · Sculptural Structuralism — Navarro Baldeweg, Susana Solano, Cristina Iglesias
tracks.where: Room 11, the first room along the back of the floor, beyond Room 10. Find a long pine table, about nine and a half metres, carrying thirty-one separate sculptures of wood, brass, bronze, rope, lead, marble and brick.
tracks.what: Juan Navarro Baldeweg, La mesa (The Table), 1974–2005, installation of 31 sculptures from the series Gravity and Balance on an Oregon pine table, 200 x 225 x 950 cm. Also: Susana Solano, No te pases, con escalera de emergencia (Take It Easy, with Emergency Ladder); Cristina Iglesias, Sin título (Untitled); Anthony Caro, Table Piece CCXXXII. The Dance, 1975; Tony Cragg, Mountain Nature; Sergi Aguilar, Tronc-Espai-Terra-Eina (16), 1974.
tracks.listen: Route II begins: thirty years of balancing acts on one table, and the moment Spanish sculpture caught the world's eye.

tracks.title: Room 12 · Extra · Cold Auras — Juan Luis Moraza
tracks.where: Room 12, along the back of the floor between Rooms 11 and 13. Look down: a square on the floor, four metres a side, made of thousands of resin shoe heels set out in a grid, from flat children's heels to tall stilettos.
tracks.what: Juan Luis Moraza, Éxtasis, estatus, estatua (Ecstasy, Status, Statue), 1994, installation of 2,496 resin heels, 12 x 400 x 400 cm. Also in the room: Pepe Espaliú, Santos (Saints); Ángeles Marco, Salto al vacío (Leap into the Void).
tracks.listen: A floor of 2,496 heels as a monument to pedestals, and the critic who named this room.

tracks.title: Room 13 · New Materialisms — Teresa Solar, Tunnelling Machine
tracks.where: In Room 13, 'New Materialisms', find the big clay sculpture, more than three metres from end to end: a clay body on a steel structure, with two resin limbs. The label calls it Tuneladora, Tunnelling Machine.
tracks.what: Teresa Solar, Tuneladora (Tunnelling Machine), 2022, clay, resin, varnish and steel, 320 × 75 × 115 cm, long-term loan of Fundación Museo Reina Sofía (donation of TBA21). Also in the room: June Crespo, Helmets; Itziar Okariz, Body Building; Sergio Prego, Home (Hogar), 2001.
tracks.listen: A tunnelling machine made of earth, and what the room means by 'new materialisms'.

tracks.title: Room 14 · Extra · Ángela de la Cruz — Nothing Under a Chair
tracks.where: In Room 14, 'Relationalities: Performative Operations with Alien Bodies', at the corner of the building. Look low: an ordinary chair with a large crumpled canvas pushed underneath it, under a metre high in all.
tracks.what: Ángela de la Cruz, Nothing Under a Chair, 1999, chair, canvas and paint, 79 × 55 × 55 cm, recent acquisition. Room 14 context: Bestué-Vives, Acciones en casa (Actions at Home); Álvaro Perdices, Jakintza.
tracks.listen: Why a painting ended up under a chair, and what it is waiting for.

tracks.title: Room 15 · Institutional Genealogy — ARCO, the museum's own story, and Chillida's logo
tracks.where: In Room 15, 'Institutional Genealogy', the first room of Route III. Look for Paz Muro's photographs of herself as a bride, Tino Calabuig's documentary ARCO 82 on a screen, and a tiny gold piece by Chillida, about five centimetres across.
tracks.what: Paz Muro, Paz Muro, nuevamente desposada con el Arte Contemporáneo Transvanguardista (Paz Muro, Newly Wed to Trans-Avant-Garde Contemporary Art), 17 February 1982, various techniques, photographs by Pablo Pérez-Mínguez. Tino Calabuig, ARCO 82, 1982, colour video with sound, 36 min. Guillermo Pérez Villalta and Manolo Quejido, posters for the MEAC Spring Festival, 1981. Eduardo Chillida, Reina Sofía, 1986, lost-wax cast gold, 5.7 × 5.1 cm, private collection.
tracks.listen: An artist marries contemporary art at the first ARCO fair, and the museum looks at its own beginnings.

tracks.title: Room 16 · Extra · Videographic Cultures of the 1980s
tracks.where: Room 16, 'Videographic Cultures of the 1980s: The Sublime Image', a small room of screens between Room 15 and Room 18. Look for Tino Calabuig's film of Guernica's journey, and a framed ink drawing of curved black shapes by Chillida.
tracks.what: Room 16 works: Tino Calabuig, Guernica, 1992, colour video with sound; Eduardo Chillida, Sin título (Dibujo original para logotipo del Centro de Arte Reina Sofía) (Untitled [Original drawing for Reina Sofía Art Centre logo]), 1986, ink on paper, 40.3 × 27 cm; also video works by Salvador Dalí, Eugènia Balcells (Indian Circle) and Miralda (Honeymoon Top).
tracks.listen: The museum's first video show, the day Guernica arrived, and the drawing behind the museum's first logo.

tracks.title: Room 17 · A More Painted Painting — Spanish painting returns
tracks.where: In Room 17, 'A More Painted Painting', the long room on the outer side of this wing. Find the wide three-panel painting, almost two metres high and nearly four metres across: a crowd of figures posed in an imaginary courtyard that opens onto a maze-like garden.
tracks.what: Guillermo Pérez Villalta, Grupo de personas en un atrio o alegoría del arte y la vida o del presente y el futuro (Group of People in an Atrium or Allegory of Art and Life or of the Present and the Future), 1975–1976, acrylic on canvas, triptych, 193 × 373 cm. Also: Manolo Quejido, Silla y máquina de escribir (Máquina sentada en silla) (Chair and Typewriter [Machine Sat on a Chair]), 1978–1979, wooden chair and typewriter.
tracks.listen: How painting came back to Spain in the late seventies and eighties, told through one crowded group portrait.

tracks.title: Room 18 · Art and Reality in 1980s Photographic Cultures — Ouka Leele, Cristina García Rodero
tracks.where: In Room 18, 'Art and Reality in 1980s. Photographic Cultures', a large room of photographs. Look for Ouka Leele's small hand-coloured prints, about 18 by 24 centimetres, and Cristina García Rodero's black-and-white pictures from her series Hidden Spain.
tracks.what: Ouka Leele (Bárbara Allende Gil de Biedma), No Title, from the series Peluquería (Hairdresser's), 1979, gelatin silver print, hand-coloured, 18 × 24 cm. Cristina García Rodero, El rey de las margaritas (Viana do Bolo, Ourense) (The King of the Daisies [Viana do Bolo, Ourense]), 1986, from España oculta (Hidden Spain), gelatin silver print, 46.5 × 31.3 cm. Also: Koldo Chamorro, Manuel Vilariño, Marta Sentís, Clemente Bernad.
tracks.listen: Two ways out of a black-and-white past: staged colour fantasy, and a patient record of hidden Spain.

tracks.title: Room 19 · Extra · Critique of Representation — Perejaume
tracks.where: Room 19, 'Critique of Representation', a small room of seven landscapes. Look for Perejaume's Serra de Busa, a thin strip of wood and canvas on the wall, only a few centimetres high but more than three and a half metres long.
tracks.what: Perejaume, Serra de Busa, 1989, wood and canvas, 2.5 × 356 × 7 cm. Also: Bleda y Rosa, Ante la mesa del rey, Las Navas de Tolosa, verano de 1212 (At the King's Table, Las Navas de Tolosa, Summer of 1212), 1996, from the series Campos de batalla (Battlefields), chromogenic print and silk screen.
tracks.listen: A room of landscapes that question what a landscape is, from a mountain range drawn as a line to a battlefield.

tracks.title: Room 20 · The African Is at the Center — Belkis Ayón and Julie Mehretu
tracks.where: In Room 20, 'Lo afro está en el centro (The African Is at the Center)', at the far corner of the floor. Find Belkis Ayón's very large print, about two metres high and two and a half wide, and Julie Mehretu's big canvas of layered ink and acrylic marks, a little over two metres high.
tracks.what: Belkis Ayón, Perfidia (Treachery), 1998, carborundum on paper, 208 × 252 cm, long-term loan of Fundación Museo Reina Sofía. Julie Mehretu, Femenine in nine, part 4 (Femenina en nueve, parte 4), 2023, acrylic and ink on canvas, 213.4 × 243.8 cm, long-term loan of Fundación Museo Reina Sofía. Also: Juan Roberto Diago, Autorretrato (Self-Portrait), 2000; Agnes Essonti Luque, A Journey, 2024; Pocho Guimaraes, OH!!!
tracks.listen: Where the room's title comes from, and two very different artists of the African diaspora: Belkis Ayón's secret-society myth and Julie Mehretu's abstraction.

tracks.title: Room 21 · Gender Practices — Pilar Albarracín and Catherine Opie
tracks.where: In Room 21, 'Gender Practices: Social Choreographies for the New Century', the long room beside the lift tower. Find Catherine Opie's colour portraits, each sitter facing you straight on, and Pilar Albarracín's round photographs of different sizes.
tracks.what: Catherine Opie, Crystal Mason, 1994, and four more works from the series Portraits, chromogenic prints. Pilar Albarracín, Mujeres (Women), 1993, later prints 2024, digital prints on photographic paper, round, 37.7 to 59 cm in diameter. Also: Regina José Galindo, El dolor en un pañuelo (Pain in a Handkerchief), 1999.
tracks.listen: A museum admits a hard number about women artists, and Catherine Opie gives her sitters the dignity of a Holbein.

tracks.title: Nouvel roof terrace · Soto, Chirino and Negret — A Different Order
tracks.where: On the roof terrace of the Nouvel building, Floor 3. Three sculptures: Soto's Penetrable, a structure almost five metres high hung with flexible tubes; Chirino's long steel form, over four metres across; and Negret's ten red-painted aluminium columns.
tracks.what: Display 'A Different Order. Utopian Geometry and Kinetic Art'. Jesús Soto, Penetrable, 1982, painted wood and flexible PVC tubes, 485 × 787 × 867 cm. Martín Chirino, Mediterránea (10) (Mediterranean [10]), 1971, welded and polished stainless steel sheet, 180 × 425 × 110 cm. Edgar Negret, Vigilante rojo (Red Watchman), 1979, painted aluminium sheet, 182 × 222 × 163 cm, donated by the artist in 1983.
tracks.listen: Three sculptures that only work when you move: a space to walk into, a steel wave, and a red watchman.

tracks.title: Closing — from Guernica to now
tracks.where: Anywhere on the Nouvel roof terrace, Floor 3, or anywhere in the museum if the terrace is closed. Nothing to find: a moment to look back over the visit.
tracks.what: No single work. Recalls Picasso, Guernica, 1937, Room 205.10; Tino Calabuig, Guernica, 1992, Room 16; Room 15, 'Institutional Genealogy'; Room 21's room text; Jesús Soto, Penetrable, Nouvel roof terrace.
tracks.listen: How Guernica's arrival shaped this museum, and why the visit ends with you.
